Initial native harness tests 20/22; both wire tests expected Connection: close but existing finite-maxSockets agent sends keep-alive. Corrected assertions after observing both modes, with no transport change. Final focused 126/126.

conclusion: Both modes reproduce matching prerender deadline/settled-native/reported-commit/500-indeterminate failures at actual concurrency twelve. Shared client/server process placement is not necessary. Separate placement has fewer failures in this bounded series but greater server callback lateness and preflight elapsed maxima; a specific interference mechanism, sufficiency, statistical significance and root cause remain unestablished.
limitations: Single host, small blocked alternating series, no universal threshold or statistical significance claim. Separate client adds an OS process and startup/IPC before/after measurement, changing scheduling and possibly GC/OS contention; those effects are not independently controlled.

Client performance timestamps are process-relative; compute overlap within each process only, never subtract client and server timestamps. Server sampler/progress/provider/publication observations are always captured in the server process.

50ms sampler tails are incomplete; pending lateness is a lower bound. Largest observed zero-check intervals are conservative, not exact maxima. Awaited intervals and SQLite preflight include continuation/lifecycle/filesystem waits, not CPU measurements.
Per-request native-stage aggregates overlap other intervals; synchronous SQLite transaction timings include open/setup/transaction/close. They do not measure CPU or prove provider blame.
Reported commit and server publication do not prove client receipt. All measured responses independently reached client end; failed mutations are still indeterminate and never retried.
nextExperiment: Keep the separate client, SQLite and actual concurrency twelve fixed; use bounded server-side continuation checkpoints around the measured SQLite preflight awaits to distinguish filesystem/lifecycle waiting from Page continuation scheduling. Do not alter deadlines, authority or transaction semantics.
